items.title: Lars Edegran Interview, 1965-09-27
items.q: Handy was there playing one night. It's very good. John Handy.

ctx.x: What about saxophones? Like any of them?
Handy was there playing one night. It's very good. John Handy.

items.title: Lars Edegran Interview, 1965-09-27
items.q: But D-John he like that stuff. He like to play the blues.

ctx.x: What do you mean? What part?

Like when we played this Bugle Ball March. March or something like that. I think that fits in a lot better. And you also get the bands to play better if you play these songs because they don't know these songs so well. They can't play too many bop phrases on them. They stick more to the melody line because it's more complex. I guess that's the reason why they play the blues because if they play the blues they can't play anything on that. They know that they can play anything on it. They don't have to play brass…
Well the people seem to like him.
